We can calculate $\frac{18{x}^{2}+27x}{6x-1}$ using synthetic division.

For synthetic division to work, we need the coefficient of $x$ in the denominator to be equal to $1.$ So first, we factor the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{18{x}^{2}+27x}{6x-1} & =\frac{18{x}^{2}+27x}{6(x-\frac{1}{6})} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot \frac{18{x}^{2}+27x}{(x-\frac{1}{6})}\end{aligned}
$$

Carrying out the synthetic division process on $\frac{18{x}^{2}+27x}{(x-\frac{1}{6})}$, we arrive at the following:

|  | ${x}^{2}$ | ${x}^{1}$ | ${x}^{0}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\frac{1}{6}$ | $18$ | $27$ | $0$ |
|  | $↓$ | $3$ | $5$ |
|  | $18$ | $30$ | $5$ |

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{6}\cdot \frac{18{x}^{2}+27x}{(x-\frac{1}{6})} & =\frac{1}{6}(18x+30+\frac{5}{(x-\frac{1}{6})}) \\  & =3x+5+\frac{5}{6x-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, our final result is

$$
\frac{18{x}^{2}+27x}{6x-1}=3x+5+\frac{5}{6x-1}.
$$
